title: "When Gitea or Forgejo Fits"

# When Gitea or Forgejo Fits

After this page you can decide whether this shape is the forge for the job in front of you.

## Choose it when

The requirement is Git hosting for a desk, a course, or a company that can name every user. You want issues and pull requests, you can live with CI as a webhook or a separate runner, and you would rather administer one data directory than a platform of services.

Forgejo is the default in this book for that job:

- the steward is a non-profit, and the license from v9 on is GPL-3.0-or-later
- 15.0 is a long-term line (security support through 15 July 2027)
- Codeberg is the same software, operated by someone else, when you do not want a server (chapter 29)

Gitea is the right lightweight forge when MIT is the constraint, or when a support contract with Gitea Ltd is the constraint. The operator experience is the sibling of Forgejo, not a different architecture.

Run it yourself when the repositories must stay on a machine you control. Use Codeberg when the code can live on a public community forge and you only need an account.

## Choose something else when

- You need merge trains, a built-in registry, dependency scanning, and GitLab CI on day one. That is chapter 24, and it is a larger machine.
- Review must be a stack of patchsets with a Change-Id. That is Gerrit (chapter 27), not a pull-request UI with a different coat of paint.
- The company standard is already GitHub or GitLab.com and the lock-in discussion in chapter 22 has been accepted. A second forge “for practice” is this lab. A second forge “for production beside the real one” is two metadata stores and one confused team.
- You expect two nodes to share one SQLite file and call it high availability. Stop at the previous page and read chapter 37 before you draw that diagram.

## A decision you can write down

```text
small team, self-hosted, free-software forge  →  Forgejo 15 LTS
small team, MIT or a Gitea contract           →  Gitea 1.27
hosted community, no server to patch          →  Codeberg
CI and registry inside the installer          →  GitLab
```

Whichever line you pick, the developer workflow does not restart. `desk-api` is still a repository, the remote is still a URL, and force-push rules from chapter 11 still apply on `main`. Part V is what changes when you are the operator of that URL for other people: identity, branch protection, and backups. The binary will not do those for you.
